newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila c.bank considers more foreign bank help.
newsitem.headline: Manila c.bank considers more foreign bank help.

text.p: Philippine central bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Tuesday he was considering offers made by foreign banks to boost the bank's dollar reserves after the peso came under renewed pressure.
"We are still studying the offers," Singson told Reuters when asked whether the central bank would accept such financial assistance.
Singson confirmed a report that ING Bank had deposited $500 million with the central bank for one year with an interest rate based on the prevailing London Interbank Offered Rate.
Nine other banks have offered financial assistance after the central bank's dollar reserves were drained in early July in an eventually futile attempt to defend the peso against speculators.
These are the Bank of Tokyo, Goldman Sachs, Salomon Brothers, Merrill Lynch, Nomura Securities, JP Morgan, ABN Amro, Chase Manhatan and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Singson said the offers vary in volume and terms, but declined to give details.
Earlier, Singson said the policy-making Monetary Board was considering measures to prevent any further fall in the peso.

The peso closed at 30.14 on Monday, or 14 percent below its level prior to the July 11 de facto devaluation when the central bank was forced to give in to a wave of speculative attacks on its currency.
Peso-dollar trading was suspended on Tuesday after heavy rains brought the capital to a halt.
